content.title: About
content.content: Iceberg lettuce is a crisp, leafy vegetable with tight, light‑green heads. It is grown in temperate climates and is widely used in fresh salads, sandwiches, and as a garnish. The leaves have a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a high water content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Iceberg gets its name from the dense, crunchy heads that resemble ice.
It is composed of more than 95 % water, making it a very low‑calorie food.
Iceberg leaves are often used as edible “plates” for appetizers and dips.
Unlike many leafy greens, iceberg stores well and stays crisp when kept properly.
Ancestors of modern iceberg lettuce were cultivated in ancient Rome.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: One cup of shredded iceberg provides about 10 kcal, ideal for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and folate
items.content: These nutrients support vision, immunity, and cell growth.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Lettuce supplies lutein and zeaxanthin, which protect the eyes from UV damage.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Its high water content helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Raw leafy greens can be contaminated with Salmonella or Listeria; thorough washing is recommended before consumption.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may experience lettuce allergy, resulting in itching or swelling.

items.title: Low nutrient density
items.content: Compared with darker leafy greens, iceberg provides fewer vitamins and minerals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Iceberg is typically eaten raw in salads, sandwiches, and wraps. Leaves can serve as a base for “boats” filled with seafood, cheese, or vegetables. For a softer texture, briefly blanch the leaves in hot water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the whole head in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or wrapped in a paper towel. When kept properly, it stays crisp for up to 10 days. Remove any wilted leaves to extend freshness.
